title: Calcium Lactate (Food Grade)
description: Calcium fortification agent and firming agent for food processing.

details.longDescription:
Calcium lactate (E327) is the calcium salt of lactic acid, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC as the pentahydrate (C6H10CaO6·5H2O, CAS 5743-47-5), a white crystalline powder with about 13% calcium, readily soluble in water and neutral in taste, in 25 kg bags and drums from stock in Muscat. It meets the E327 specification and the US FDA GRAS listing, and every lot ships with a certificate of analysis and food-grade documentation.

Why food processors choose it. Calcium lactate dissolves completely and tastes clean, which is why it fortifies clear beverages, juices, sports and electrolyte drinks and flavoured waters where calcium carbonate would settle and leave a chalky mouthfeel; typical use runs 0.2–0.5% of the beverage, up to about 1% for high-calcium claims, within the salt's solubility of roughly 5–9 g per 100 mL. It is well absorbed, so it is also a calcium source in dairy enrichment, nutritional supplements and pharmaceutical calcium tablets.

As a firming agent it keeps canned and frozen fruit and vegetables, pickles and pre-cut fresh produce crisp: calcium ions cross-link pectin in the plant cell walls, so slices and pieces hold their shape through heat processing; dips of 0.5–1% are typical for fresh-cut fruit. In jams, jellies and low-sugar fruit preparations it supplies the calcium that sets low-methoxyl pectin and alginate gels, and in baking it is a component of some leavening systems and a dough improver.

Formulation notes: calcium lactate is compatible with most acids and flavours but will precipitate with phosphates, carbonates and sulphates at high concentrations, so add it after other salts and check clarity in a bench trial. It is also the calcium source in spherification with sodium alginate. The pentahydrate loses water if stored warm and dry, so keep bags closed and below 30 °C; it is non-hazardous.

Technical-grade citric acid (also called industrial-grade) is manufactured to lower purity standards at reduced cost and may contain higher levels of heavy metal impurities and microbial contamination. Technical-grade citric acid must never be used in food or pharmaceutical production as the impurity profile is not controlled to a level safe for human consumption. title: Formaldehyde 40% (Technical Grade)
description: Industrial disinfectant, fumigant and preservative for empty facilities and non-food-contact equipment.

details.longDescription:
Formaldehyde 40%, sold as formalin, is a 37–40% solution of formaldehyde (CH2O, CAS 50-00-0) in water stabilised with 10–15% methanol to stop it polymerising into paraformaldehyde. Global Chemicals LLC supplies the technical grade in 30 L containers and 200 L drums from stock in Muscat for industrial disinfection, fumigation and preservation. It is not a food-contact product: it is used to disinfect empty facilities and equipment that are then aired and rinsed before use.

Where it is used. Poultry houses and hatcheries are fumigated with formaldehyde between flocks, classically by generating the gas from formalin and potassium permanganate or by heating formalin, in a sealed, empty building that is ventilated thoroughly before birds return; cold stores, warehouses, storage tanks and vehicles are disinfected the same way. Formaldehyde kills bacteria, viruses, fungi and spores, which is why it remains in use where other disinfectants cannot reach every surface. Outside disinfection it preserves textiles, leather and biological specimens, and it is the feedstock of urea-, phenol- and melamine-formaldehyde resins.

Health and regulation. Formaldehyde is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1) and in the EU as a presumed carcinogen (Carc. 1B), suspected mutagen, skin sensitiser and skin-corrosive substance; it is toxic by inhalation, ingestion and skin contact, and the vapour irritates eyes and airways at very low concentrations. It must be handled only by trained staff, in well-ventilated areas or with full-face respiratory protection with formaldehyde cartridges, chemical goggles, nitrile or butyl gloves and coveralls. Fumigated buildings must be empty of people and animals and ventilated until the level falls below the workplace exposure limit before re-entry. Supply is to registered business accounts.

Storage: keep drums closed, upright, at 15–25 °C, out of sunlight and away from oxidisers, acids, alkalis and ammonia; at low temperatures (below about 5–10 °C for methanol-stabilised grades) paraformaldehyde precipitates as a white sediment, and the methanol makes the solution flammable (flash point about 50–64 °C closed cup depending on methanol content; use the value on the safety data sheet). Every delivery carries a certificate of analysis giving formaldehyde and methanol content, and a GHS safety data sheet.

Delivery is same day within Muscat and Rusayl Industrial Area, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road across the GCC with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the pack size, quantity and intended use.

title: Limestone (Food Grade)
description: Food-grade calcium source and pH adjuster for food and beverage processing.

details.longDescription:
Ground limestone is natural calcium carbonate (CaCO3, CAS 471-34-1); the standard grade runs 95–98% CaCO3, giving 38–39% calcium, and material for food use (E170) must reach at least 98% CaCO3 on a dried basis, so ask for the food-grade certificate where it will reach food. It comes with low heavy metals, at least 85% whiteness and particle sizes from 50 to 200 mesh, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC in 25 kg and 50 kg bags and bulk from stock in Muscat. A 10% slurry reads about pH 9, so it neutralises acidity gently and without the overshoot of lime or caustic.

Food, feed and agriculture. Feed mills use it as the main calcium source in poultry and livestock rations: layer hens need coarse particles of 2–4 mm for strong eggshells, a different size from the 50–200 mesh powder listed here, so specify the layer grade when ordering; broiler and ruminant feeds take the fine grades. Food processors use it as a calcium fortificant and acidity regulator (E170) and as a neutralising agent for acidic process streams and wastes. Beet sugar factories and sugar refineries burn limestone to make the quicklime and carbon dioxide used to purify juice by carbonatation. In agriculture it is the standard liming material for acidic soils and growing media, and a calcium source where gypsum is not wanted.

Industrial uses. Water-treatment plants use limestone contactors and dosing to remineralise and stabilise desalinated water, and to neutralise acidic effluent; flue-gas desulphurisation scrubbers use limestone slurry to capture sulphur dioxide; and construction uses the coarser grades as filler and aggregate. For high-brightness industrial grades in plastics, paint and paper, see the calcium carbonate page.

Choosing the grade: ask for food or feed grade where the product will reach food or animal feed, and specify the particle size for the job, because reaction speed and handling depend on fineness. The powder is non-hazardous; avoid breathing dust, wear a dust mask when tipping bags, and keep bags dry, as damp limestone cakes and flows poorly. Every lot carries a certificate of analysis giving CaCO3 content, particle size, moisture and heavy metals, and a safety data sheet.

faqs.question: What is food-grade caustic soda and how is it used in the food industry?
faqs.answer: Food-grade caustic soda (sodium hydroxide, NaOH) is a high-purity alkaline solution that meets food safety standards including codex alimentarius and FDA 21 CFR 184.1763 specifications, with strict limits on heavy metals, chloride, and iron impurities. In the food and beverage industry, it is used primarily for clean-in-place (CIP) cleaning of production equipment — tanks, pipelines, fillers, and pasteurisers — where it dissolves protein soils, fats, and starchy deposits that accumulate during processing. It is also used in food processing itself: for pretzel crust formation (lye dipping), olive curing, noodle making, and pH adjustment in beverages. faqs.question: What is the typical CIP concentration of caustic soda for food plant cleaning in Oman?
faqs.answer: For clean-in-place (CIP) cleaning in food plants, caustic soda is typically used at 0.5–2.0% w/w concentration depending on the soil type and equipment being cleaned. Dairy CIP programmes (for milk, cheese, and yoghurt plants) commonly use 0.8–1.5% caustic at 70–80°C for 10–20 minute contact time to dissolve protein and fat soils. Beverage lines and fruit juice plants use lower concentrations of 0.5–1.0% at 60–75°C. Brewery and winery CIP may use 1.0–2.0% for heavily soiled fermentation vessels. In Oman's hot climate, the higher ambient temperatures mean pre-rinse water is already warm, slightly reducing the heating energy needed. However, concentrated caustic at elevated temperatures significantly increases stainless steel corrosion rates, so precise concentration control is important. Global Chemicals LLC supplies caustic soda with test kit support for accurate on-site concentration measurement during CIP operations.

faqs.question: What is food-grade sodium bicarbonate used for in the food and beverage industry?
faqs.answer: Food-grade sodium bicarbonate (baking soda, NaHCO₃) is a leavening agent, pH regulator, and buffering agent widely used across the food and beverage industry. faqs.question: What is food-grade sodium hypochlorite and how is it used in food processing?
faqs.answer: Food-grade sodium hypochlorite is a high-purity chlorine solution produced from food-safe feedstocks, with heavy metal and impurity limits meeting food safety regulations. It is one of the most widely used disinfectants in food processing worldwide — applied as a surface sanitiser, equipment disinfectant, produce wash, and water disinfectant in CIP and COP (clean-out-of-place) programmes. At concentrations of 50–200 ppm free chlorine, it rapidly kills pathogens including Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria, and Campylobacter on contact surfaces and fresh produce. In Oman's fish processing, meat processing, vegetable packing, and catering sectors, sodium hypochlorite is used daily for sanitising work surfaces, knives, cutting boards, crates, and conveyor belts. It must be used at the correct concentration — too low is ineffective, too high risks chemical contamination and accelerates corrosion. Global Chemicals LLC supplies food-grade sodium hypochlorite with concentration certification.

faqs.question: What concentration of sodium hypochlorite is safe for fruit and vegetable washing in Oman?
faqs.answer: For fresh produce washing, the internationally recommended sodium hypochlorite concentration is 50–200 ppm free available chlorine (FAC) in the wash water, with typical practice in fresh-cut produce operations using 100–150 ppm FAC. At this concentration, the chlorinated wash kills surface pathogens on vegetables and fruit and a potable-water rinse afterwards keeps residual chlorine low (follow the residue limits of the local food-safety authority). The wash solution must be maintained at pH 6.5–7.5 for maximum hypochlorous acid (HOCl) availability — at pH above 8.0, hypochlorite ion (OCl⁻) predominates and antimicrobial efficacy drops by 80%. In Oman's hot climate, produce temperatures can be high, which accelerates chlorine degradation and requires more frequent solution replacement. Global Chemicals LLC supplies food-grade sodium hypochlorite with test strips and photometric kits for accurate FAC monitoring in food operations.

title: White Salt (Food Grade)
description: Food-grade refined sodium chloride for seasoning and preservation.

details.longDescription:
Food-grade white salt (refined sodium chloride, NaCl, CAS 7647-14-5) is supplied by Global Chemicals LLC at 99.5% minimum purity with heavy metals below 10 ppm, as clean white crystalline granules in fine, medium and coarse grain sizes, iodised or non-iodised, in 1 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg bags from stock in Muscat to food manufacturers, meat and fish processors, bakeries, dairies, restaurants and catering companies across Oman. Each lot ships with a certificate of analysis and the food-safety documentation buyers need for their own audits; the laboratory reagent and industrial grades are listed separately.

Which grain to order. Fine salt dissolves fastest and is the seasoning and bakery salt, dosed at about 1.8–2.2% of flour weight in bread, where it controls fermentation and strengthens gluten as well as seasoning the loaf. Medium grain is the general processing salt for soups, sauces, snacks and ready meals. Coarse salt is for brines, pickling, curing, fish salting and cheese making, where slow dissolution and even coverage matter; cheese makers salt curds or brine wheels with it, and meat processors build curing brines from it with the nitrite cure added separately. Fermentation of vegetables, olives and sauces uses the non-iodised grade, because iodine can inhibit the culture and darken the product. Iodised salt carries the standard iodine fortification for table and household use.

Why refined: raw sea salt carries magnesium and calcium chlorides that make it bitter and hygroscopic, plus sand and organic matter; refining removes them, which is what gives this salt its clean taste, white colour, free flow and consistent brine strength.

Storage and handling: salt is not hazardous, but it is corrosive to mild steel and absorbs moisture in humid air, so keep bags closed, dry and off the floor, use plastic or stainless equipment for brines, and rotate stock. It is non-perishable.

Delivery is same day within Muscat, next day to Sohar, two to three days to Salalah and Duqm, and by road to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain with a certificate of origin. Request a quote with the grain size, iodised or not, bag size and monthly volume.
